# `Q-11-2` — SimpleTable is not supported

> A Lua filter used the legacy pre-pandoc-2.10 SimpleTable API, which
> Quarto does not implement.

## What this means

Pandoc has had two table representations. The original `SimpleTable`
was replaced in pandoc 2.10 by the richer `pandoc.Table`, which can
express row and column spans, multiple header rows, table bodies, and
a caption. `SimpleTable` survives in pandoc only as a compatibility
shim.

Quarto does not carry that shim. Three names are affected:

- `pandoc.SimpleTable`
- `pandoc.utils.to_simple_table`
- `pandoc.utils.from_simple_table`

A filter calling any of them stops with this error.

## Why this happens

- **A filter written against a pandoc 2.9-or-earlier tutorial.** Much
  of the Lua filter material online predates the 2.10 change.
- **A filter copied from a long-lived project** that was written before
  2.10 and kept working in pandoc through the shim.
- **Round-tripping to simplify table handling** — `to_simple_table`
  followed by `from_simple_table` was a common way to avoid the full
  `Table` structure.

## How to fix

Work with `pandoc.Table` directly. A `Table` element has these fields:

| Field       | Holds                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `caption`   | a `Caption`                                    |
| `colspecs`  | alignment and width per column                 |
| `head`      | a `TableHead`                                  |
| `bodies`    | a list of `TableBody`                          |
| `foot`      | a `TableFoot`                                  |

Reading cell contents means walking `head.rows` and each body's
`body` rows, rather than the flat `rows` list `SimpleTable` offered:

```lua
function Table(tbl)
  for _, body in ipairs(tbl.bodies) do
    for _, row in ipairs(body.body) do
      for _, cell in ipairs(row.cells) do
        -- cell.contents is a list of Blocks
      end
    end
  end
  return tbl
end
```

The structure is more verbose, but it is the only representation that
can round-trip a table without losing spans or a caption — which is
why the simple form was retired.
